Last year, Apple brought a radical multitasking overhaul to the iPad with iPadOS 26, introducing windowing. At first, that meant simpler multitasking modes — Split View and Slide Over — were removed. They did eventually return, but at the cost of users having to use the awkward new windowing system to access them. I had hoped iPadOS 27 would improve on this, but it didn't.

To be clear, I'm not entirely against the new windowing system in iPadOS 26 (and now 27). It has its place, and it works wonderfully when I'm juggling multiple apps on my 13-inch iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard. As for smaller iPads, I have mixed feelings, but it's generally acceptable.

What I don't like, however, is that aside from Stage Manager (which feels more like a feature within windowing rather than a standalone option), the only alternative is to have every app run full-screen — with no flexibility whatsoever.

What I was hoping to see

As mentioned, iPadOS 26 eventually brought back Split View and Slide Over in later betas — but only if you turned on windowing. This means that if you want simpler multitasking, you're forced to deal with all the complexity layers designed for pro users.

That's fine, of course, but it's genuinely annoying sometimes having to get the windows positioned just right to snap into Split View or Slide Over, when the process was much smoother before iPadOS 26. It's also a loss for users who enjoy windowing, because if you drag a window slightly off, it might enter Split View when you don't want it to.

Apple does let you long-press the red, yellow, or green light buttons for more precise Split View and Slide Over state toggle options, but that doesn't feel right for simple iPad usage either.

Split View and Slide Over should be part of iPadOS, but cramming them into the windowing system makes them more complex than they need to be — even a year later.

The bottom line

Ideally, iPadOS should offer two sets of multitasking: Classic and Pro. Classic would essentially open apps full-screen but offer Slide Over and Split View options; Pro would have the windowing functionality introduced in iPadOS 26. Within Pro, there should also be an option to enable/disable Stage Manager.

Top comment by G A B E 🪐

What bugs me is that Slide Over hasn't really returned. I have zero interest in Stage Manager unless I have the Magic Keyboard folio attached or an external display connected (side note, it would be nice if the iPad entered Stage Manager mode automatically when either of those is connected). I'm curious how the foldable iPhone will handle multitasking.

Overall, I feel like Apple has pushed the iPad too far in one direction, favoring Magic Keyboard/laptop-replacement users, while multitasking has suffered a bit for those who just want to use their iPad as an iPad. Adding back a 'simple' multitasking option would go a long way toward fixing this.

What are your thoughts on iPad multitasking since iPadOS 26? Let us know in the comments.
